fichas.title: Laboratory medicine
fichas.summary: Hospital laboratory areas process blood, urine, and stool samples, with a large main room for standing and seated workstations and separate specialist laboratories. Subsidiary rooms support staff, rinsing, sluicing, disinfection, and cold storage. A pneumatic delivery system provides quick connections to other departments; laboratories may also be off-site and serve several hospitals.
uses: Preparation and processing of blood, urine, and stool samples
Pneumatic delivery of samples or materials between departments
figure_refs: Figure 1: Laboratory area at the Dr. Horst Schmidt Clinics, Wiesbaden

fichas.title: Pathology department
fichas.summary: A hospital pathology department accommodates body storage and refrigeration, dissection, laying out, coffin placement and storage, and changing rooms for pathologists. Provide separate access for relatives and short road access for undertakers. The department should be separated from the service yard vicinity.
uses: Storage, refrigeration, and dissection of bodies
Laying out bodies and placing them into coffins
figure_refs: Figure 3: Pathology department at the St. Clemens Hospital, Geldern, 480 beds

fichas.title: Radiology
fichas.summary: Radiology accommodates diagnostic and therapeutic use of ionising radiation. Locate it near the outpatient department and ambulance approach; the heavy equipment favors a ground-floor or first-basement location. Room planning depends on equipment and associated technology. Patient access to radioscopy rooms includes two changing cubicles per room and a wide bed-access door. Specialized rooms and support spaces are required for angiography, computer tomography, switching, and film development. Walls and ceilings receive lead protection specified in coordination with the X-ray equipment manufacturer.
uses: Diagnostic and therapeutic application of ionising radiation
Sonography, mammography, angiography, and computer tomography
